records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 📅 Saturday, 5 September 2026 | 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 🌍 Ethiopian Airlines has filed to more than double its Addis–Kilimanjaro–Zanzibar service from 30 November. We have not seen this reported anywhere in the East African trade press yet. 1️⃣ ETHIOPIAN GOES DAILY INTO KILIMANJARO AND ZANZIBAR — FROM 30 NOVEMBER Ethiopian has filed a schedule increase on the Addis Ababa – Kilimanjaro – Zanzibar – Addis triangle: from the 3 weekly originally filed to 7 weekly, effective 30 November 2026 (AeroRoutes, published 04 September 2026). Overall Ethiopian service into those two airports rises from 17–18 weekly to 21. The rotation is ET855, a 737-800: ADD 23:00 → JRO 01:20 → ZNZ 03:30, back into ADD 07:00. Read the clock before you read the capacity. Kilimanjaro receives at 01:20 and dispatches at 02:10; Zanzibar receives at 03:30 and dispatches at 04:20. That is a connecting bank feeding the Addis wave from Europe, Asia and the Gulf — not leisure timing. What arrives with it is night transfers and 06:00 arrivals at your gate, from guests on a through-fare who will not pay a supplement for an early room. The demand side is where the caution sits. Zanzibar's arrivals growth has cooled: +19.2% year-on-year in January 2026, +4.9% in February, +3.1% in June, +9.6% in July (Office of the Chief Government Statistician, monthly releases). Seats are landing into the December–March peak faster than arrivals are currently growing. 🎯 So what: publish a priced 06:00 early-check-in policy before 30 November — you will be asked. And stress-test your peak rate strategy against arrivals growth of three per cent, not nineteen. New lift is not new demand. 🏷 Beach, Bush | 🇹🇿 | Confirmed (filing) / Inference (rate effect, ours) | impact:demand 2️⃣ 92% OF LUXURY HOTEL PHONE CALLS CAPTURE NOTHING A Revinate mystery-shopper study of 308 calls to 135 luxury and upscale properties found 92.2% captured no guest contact detail, and staff asked zero discovery questions on more than half the calls (via Hospitality Net, 4 September 2026). The sample is North American. The failure is not. Our transmission is direct. EA lodges and camps run far more enquiry by phone and WhatsApp than a European city hotel, and far more confirmed business through agents. The direct enquiry is the one channel where you own the guest record outright. Losing the name and email on nine calls in ten means paying commission twice — to whoever converts the guest this year, and again next year because you cannot reach them. 🎯 So what: mystery-shop your own reservations line this week. One call, at 19:00. If your team quotes a rate before asking for a name and an email, that is a free fix worth more than any channel-mix project you have. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | 🌍→EA | Confirmed (study) / Inference (EA read, ours) | impact:cost 📡 RADAR • 4 Sep, held — 21st Kwita Izina at Kinigi; 22 gorillas named (RDB, 4 Sep). Exhibition runs to 8 Sep: three nights of Musanze demand still open. • 5–12 Sep, running — Miss Tourism East Africa finals, Kampala. ~24 contestants: one property's group booking. Do not lift Kampala BAR on it. • 11 Sep, 16:59 EDT — the CDC order rerouting Uganda- and South Sudan-origin arrivals expires. Watch for renewal or lapse. • ~14 Sep — EPRA fuel review; the current Kenya cycle ends 14 Sep. • 30 Nov — Ethiopian's daily JRO/ZNZ rotation begins, on today's filing. 💬 Beach operators: what does a 03:30 arrival actually cost you in transfers and early check-ins? 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Morning Brief · Sat 5 Sep 🚨 ETHIOPIAN GOES DAILY INTO ZANZIBAR AND KILIMANJARO From 30 Nov, Addis–Kilimanjaro–Zanzibar goes 3 to 7 weekly (AeroRoutes, 4 Sep). Not yet in the EA trade press. Read the clock: JRO arrives 01:20, ZNZ 03:30, both dispatch before dawn — a connecting bank, not leisure timing. → Do this: publish and price a 06:00 early check-in policy before 30 November. 📌 ALSO

records.title: Kenya is proposing to move its tourism statistics inside its tourism marketing agency. The whole region should be watching.
records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 📅 Saturday, 5 September 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 Nothing cleared the recency gate since midday. So tonight, the Bill in committee that changes who collects your levy, who decides how it is spent, and who counts your guests. 1️⃣ KENYA WOULD PUT ITS TOURISM STATISTICS INSIDE ITS TOURISM MARKETING AGENCY The Tourism (Amendment) Bill 2026 transfers the functions, assets, liabilities, pending proceedings and licences of the Tourism Research Institute to the Kenya Tourism Board, ending TRI as a separate body; staff go to the Public Service Commission. The Tourism Finance Corporation goes the same way. The Tourism Fund keeps collecting hotel and restaurant levies, with the Cabinet Secretary overseeing management, and its mandate widens to research, data, events, county matching grants — and "marketing and branding". It would also draw proceeds from the Air Passenger Service Charge. (The Kenya Times, 21 August 2026, on the Departmental Committee sitting of 20 August.) What everyone is missing. The debate is about institutional power — KATO's Fred Odek warned of a "data vacuum"; Hospitality EQ's Barry Clemens flagged concentration risk (Tourism Update, 26 August 2026). The operator issue is narrower. You fund this through the levy. TRI's arrivals series — 2.7 million international visitors in 2025, up about 9% (TRI Annual Tourism Sector Performance Report 2025, reported 2 April 2026) — is what the whole region prices off, because nothing more granular is published free anywhere in East Africa. Move it inside the agency paid to make Kenya look good and it stops being usable in a lender's feasibility study. Inference, labelled: that discount lands in credit committees, not headlines. And the archive is physical. TRI's reports sit on TRI's own domain. Dissolve the institution and the domain goes with it. 🎯 So what: Download every TRI report your models cite — tonight — and write the source and retrieval date into the document. If you submit during public participation, ask for series continuity and a protected archive, not just a directorate. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | 🇰🇪 (regional read 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼) | Confirmed (Bill contents, as reported) / Inference (effects) | impact:strategy 2️⃣ STILL TRUE — TANZANIA AND ZANZIBAR ARE STILL TWO LEVELS APART No advisory movement on any of the five markets today. The US holds Tanzania and Zanzibar at Level 3, raised from Level 2 on 31 October 2025 on an "unrest" indicator (verified vs travel.state.gov, 4 August 2026). The UK has the same ground at Level 1, advising against travel only within 20km of the Cabo Delgado border. Ten months, no movement. 🎯 So what: A client quoting "Level 3" is quoting a 2025 decision. Send the FCDO page rather than discounting a beach rate. 🏷 Beach, Bush | 🇹🇿 | Confirmed | impact:demand 3️⃣ COST PULSE — NINE DAYS TO EPRA, THEN THE VAT CLIFF Kenyan diesel holds at KSh 217.86/L to 14 September 2026, roughly KSh 14 above what landed costs implied, because diesel users are cross-subsidising petrol (EPRA notice / Business Daily, 14 August 2026). The bigger date is 14 October, when the 8% VAT rate on petroleum expires. 🎯 So what: Refuse any supplier fuel surcharge before 14 September — the landed-cost figure kills the argument. 🏷 Bush, City | 🇰🇪 | Confirmed | impact:margin 📅 MICE WATCH: Miss Tourism East Africa 2026 runs 5–12 September in Kampala. records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 📅 Friday, 4 September 2026 | 🇹🇿 🇰🇪 🇷🇼 Tanzania is still banned from EU skies. Much of the trade has been told otherwise for a year. 1️⃣ TANZANIA IS STILL ON THE EU BAN LIST. THE TRADE THINKS IT ISN'T. The Commission's 48th update of the EU Air Safety List (DG MOVE, 9 June 2026) still bans every Tanzanian-certified airline — one of 16 states listed for inadequate regulator oversight, not aircraft faults. Kyrgyzstan came off the same list entirely, so it is a two-way door. Yet ATTA's library still carries "Tanzanian Airlines to Resume Flights to Europe After EU Safety Ban Lifted", 15 September 2025, sourced to Tuko. Wrong then, still circulating. Separately, TCAA posted a notice headlined "TCAA and EU reaffirm commitment to strengthen aviation safety oversight" (tcaa.go.tz, 4 September 2026; seen 06:23 EAT, no press coverage found). The notice exists — the page would not render for us, so we make no claim on its contents. 🎯 So what: the ban is on the authority, not the fleet, and guests will not draw that line for you. Put one written sentence in your agent sheet saying domestic Tanzanian flights are unaffected — and stop the "ban lifted" story where you find it. 🏷 Bush, Beach, City | 🇹🇿 | Confirmed (list) / Early signal (TCAA notice) | impact:risk 2️⃣ ARUSHA GOES 24 HOURS — THE COMPULSORY OVERNIGHT ENDS ATCL chief executive Eng. Peter Ulanga says Arusha Airport begins round-the-clock operations within two weeks, after a lighting upgrade cleared night flights (Daily News Tanzania, 2 September 2026). Daily capacity rises from about 200 passengers to 300, on Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar routes. The stated purpose is evening safari arrivals: guests no longer need to sleep in Arusha before continuing. It is also positioned for Tanzania's co-hosting of AFCON 2027. 🎯 So what: Arusha town has sold a captive night for years. From mid-September that night is optional, and same-day bush-to-beach moves it to Zanzibar. Rebuild the Arusha rate case on a reason to stay — this month. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | 🇹🇿 | Confirmed | impact:watch 3️⃣ TURKANA GETS A TEN-YEAR PLAN AND A FUNDED PARTNER KWS formalised a management partnership with Archipelagus on 29 August 2026 covering Sibiloi and Central Island National Parks (KWS press release, Aug 2026; via ATTA, 3 September). It anchors the Lake Turkana National Parks Management Plan 2026–2036 across more than 6,000 km² of parks and community rangelands, currently on UNESCO's "In Danger" list. First moves: a Sibiloi headquarters, a joint operations centre, ranger outposts on real-time monitoring. Later: grassland restoration, phased reintroduction of reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra and black rhino, and nature-based tourism. 🎯 So what: Kenya's emptiest circuit just got a decade-long plan and a funded partner, with almost no bed stock in it. Read it if you are looking at concessions. Do not put Turkana in a brochure yet. 🏷 Bush | 🇰🇪 | Confirmed | impact:demand 📡 RADAR • Today, 4 Sep — 21st Kwita Izina, Kinigi. 22 gorillas named, total 460 (RDB, 2 Sep). Exhibition to 8 Sep: hold rate across the window, not the ceremony night alone. • 5–12 Sep — Miss Tourism East Africa finals, Kampala. ~24 contestants: one house's group booking, not city compression. • ~16 Sep — Arusha night operations live, on ATCL's two-week timeline. • 16 Sep — Kenya's High Court hears the US$50,000 travel-health insurance petition; suspended until then. • ~26 Sep — the three-week KAWU arbitration window from the 1 September deal closes. 💬 Selling Tanzania into Europe: has any agent raised the EU list with you this year? 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Morning Brief · Fri 4 Sep 📌 TANZANIA STILL BANNED FROM EU SKIES The EU's 48th Air Safety List update (9 Jun 2026) still bans every Tanzanian-certified airline — on regulator oversight, not aircraft. A "ban lifted" story from Sept 2025 is still circulating.

records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 📅 Thursday, 3 September 2026 | 🇺🇬 🇰🇪 🇷🇼 🇹🇿 Uganda got its all-clear eight days ago. Washington hasn't noticed. 1️⃣ US STILL HAS UGANDA AT "DO NOT TRAVEL" — OVER AN ENDED OUTBREAK We read the State Department's Uganda page this morning. It is still Level 4 — Do Not Travel , date issued 4 June 2026 , with Health among its four indicators. The advisory history is explicit: Uganda was moved from Level 3 to Level 4 on 17 May 2026 "due to the Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease outbreak in Ituri Province in the DRC." The live page still describes mass-gathering restrictions in Kampala and 21-day quarantine for DRC arrivals. Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the outbreak over on 28 July . WHO certified it on 26 August after the full 42-day countdown. The advisory has not been re-issued in 91 days. The UK, by contrast, advises against travel to no part of Uganda. State's own text links out to a CDC health notice filed under Level 2. We haven't seen this gap reported anywhere yet. 🎯 So what: Stop waiting for the downgrade before you sell. Put the WHO 26 August certification and the FCDO position in your agent pack this week — you are selling against a US document, not a disease. 🏷 Bush, City | 🇺🇬 | Confirmed | impact:risk 2️⃣ AND HERE IS WHY THE DOWNGRADE MAY NOT COME DRC's health ministry put the outbreak at 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths on 2 September (data to 31 August) — past 3,000 dead, and the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded. Ituri alone carries 5,065 cases and 2,305 deaths. WHO's 14 August notice called it the fastest-expanding Ebola outbreak on record, CFR 46.8%, with no licensed vaccine for this strain. 🎯 So what: Washington's stated grounds were always Ituri, not Uganda. Inference, not fact — but budget Level 4 through Q4 and price US groups accordingly rather than holding inventory for a rebound. 🏷 Bush, City | 🇺🇬 🇷🇼 | Confirmed | impact:risk 3️⃣ 8.9 MILLION PASSENGERS THROUGH A 7.5 MILLION AIRPORT KAA has disclosed that JKIA is running beyond design capacity and risks losing share to Bishoftu, Bugesera and Msalato (The EastAfrican, 2 September). The $900m upgrade to 25m passengers is tendered to CRBC but unfunded — ~$630m is still being arranged via TDB and AFC. 🎯 So what: Nairobi's hub premium has a visible expiry date. If your 2027 corporate rate card assumes JKIA connectivity, hedge it now with direct-arrival product. 🏷 City | 🇰🇪 | Confirmed | impact:watch 4️⃣ $800 TO FLY MOMBASA–ENTEBBE KATO's Coast representative Patrick Kamanga put the fare at nearly $800 — "equivalent to travelling to Europe" (The EastAfrican, 2 September). Uganda sent 234,556 visitors to Kenya in 2025. M-Pesa and MoMo still cannot pay each other's tills across the border. 🎯 So what: Your best-converting regional guest cannot pay you on their phone. Add a Ugandan mobile-money option at the coast before the 26–27 October summit talks about it. 🏷 Beach, City | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 | Confirmed | impact:demand 📡 RADAR • 4 Sep — Kwita Izina, Kinigi; exhibition runs to 8 Sep (RDB) • 5–12 Sep — Miss Tourism East Africa finals, Kampala • 14 Sep — EPRA fuel cycle closes; new Kenyan prices 15 Sep • 27 Sep — EU EmpCo directive applies; "eco-lodge" claims need evidence • 26–27 Oct — EAC regional tourism summit 💬 Are your US agents still quoting the Level 4, or have they moved on? 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Morning Brief · Thu 3 Sep 🚨 US STILL SAYS "DO NOT TRAVEL" TO UGANDA We read the page this morning: Level 4, issued 4 June, still citing Ebola — 8 days after WHO certified Uganda Ebola-free on 26 Aug. records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 📅 Tuesday, 1 September 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 The JKIA strike is over. Read the agreement, not the headline — it sets its own expiry date, and it falls in three weeks. 1️⃣ KAWU CALLS OFF THE STRIKE. THE DEAL HAS A THREE-WEEK FUSE. The Kenya Aviation Workers Union signed a return-to-work agreement this morning with KCAA, the Kenya Airports Authority and Jambojet, after a meeting chaired by Transport CS Davis Chirchir. Members were sent back immediately; agency fees held by KAA go to the union at once (KBC, 1 September, 07:36 EAT). Now the fine print. The Salaries and Remuneration Commission withdrew its 28 July guidance and issued fresh parameters on 1 September — and the union recorded reservations about those parameters inside the agreement itself . The 20 July strike-notice grievances go to arbitration under the PS for Aviation within three weeks — by roughly 22 September . The Jambojet recognition dispute is parked with a court. 🎯 So what: Called off is not recovered. KBC reports passengers at JKIA since Monday; aircraft and crew are out of position, so today's arrivals are harder to plan than yesterday's. Hold rooms through tonight. Then diarise 22 September — February's settlement held five months, July's held one, and this one names its own next flashpoint. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | Kenya | Confirmed | impact:risk 2️⃣ THE FCDO DID NOT DOWNGRADE KENYA. IT ADDED AN AIRPORT NOTE. "UK warns its citizens against travel to Kenya," ran the local headline yesterday (The Kenya Times, 31 August). We read the page. What the FCDO added on 31 August is one operational paragraph: industrial action is affecting airport operations, check with your airline. The advise-against-all-travel geography is unchanged and years old — Mandera; Tarbaj and Wajir East (except Wajir Town) and Wajir within 60km of Somalia; Garissa except Garissa Town, Lagdera and specified Balambala areas; Lamu except Lamu and Manda Islands. Ground: terrorism from Somalia-based groups (gov.uk, updated 31 August). 🎯 So what: Nairobi, Mombasa, Diani, Watamu, the Mara, Amboseli and Laikipia are not in that list and never have been. When an agent forwards you the headline, don't reassure — quote the counties back. Precision closes the booking. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | Kenya | Confirmed | impact:demand 3️⃣ KENYA 6.6%, UGANDA 4.1% — AND KENYAN DIESEL FELL. Kenya's annual inflation rose to 6.6% from 6.5%: food +9.0%, transport +15.7% , housing and utilities +3.6% (KNBS, 31 August). Uganda printed 4.1% from 4.0%, on food crops moving to 2.1% from 1.6% (UBOS, 31 August). 🎯 So what: Kenyan transport inflation ran at 15.7% in a month when average diesel fell 2.2% to KSh 219.04/litre (KNBS). The pump isn't driving it — fares and margin are. Next time a transfer operator hands you a fuel surcharge, the fuel number is on your side of the table. 🏷 City, Bush | Kenya, Uganda | Confirmed | impact:cost 📡 RADAR • KAWU arbitration deadline ~22 September — diarise it • Kwita Izina, Kinigi — ceremony 4 Sept, exhibition to 8 Sept (RDB) • Miss Tourism East Africa finals, Kampala — 5–12 Sept • CBK weekly bulletin Friday; EPRA fuel review ~14 Sept 💬 Our ledger called settlement by 6 September. It landed on the 1st. The harder question is whether 22 September holds. 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Morning Brief · Tue 1 Sep 🚨 JKIA STRIKE CALLED OFF — WITH A THREE-WEEK FUSE KAWU signed a return-to-work deal this morning. records.title: In 26 days, "eco-lodge" stops being a marketing word and becomes a legal claim
records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 📅 Tuesday, 1 September 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 Nothing cleared the recency gate since midday. So tonight, the thing 26 days out that almost nobody here has diarised. 1️⃣ ON 27 SEPTEMBER, "ECO-LODGE" STOPS BEING FREE EU Directive 2024/825 — Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition — applies from 27 September 2026 (EUR-Lex; European Commission). It bans generic green claims to EU consumers unless a recognised certification backs them: "eco-friendly", "green", "sustainable", "responsible". It bans "carbon neutral" where the claim rests on offsets outside your value chain. It bans self-made badges. Where you are based is irrelevant: per Sustainable Travel International's guide (5 August 2026), the rules bind anyone marketing to EU consumers, Africa included. What everyone is missing. Enforcement won't come from Brussels. It will come from your German agent. The EU operator reselling your lodge is squarely in scope, carries the fine risk — the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive that EmpCo amends allows maximum fines of at least 4% of turnover in the member states concerned — and reuses your copy in its brochure. Our inference, labelled as such: the Q4 contracting round brings substantiation questionnaires down the chain for the first time. And this is not a cost. It is a repricing. Conservation credentials have been commercially worthless here for twenty years because they were free to claim: a conservancy paying real lease fees competed against a lodge whose entire programme was the word "eco". From 27 September only one of them can keep saying it. 🎯 So what: Search your website tonight for "eco", "green", "sustainable", "carbon neutral". Evidence each hit, replace it with a measured fact, or delete it by 27 September. Then start a Travelife or Green Key application — both are named as legitimate schemes. 🏷 Bush, Beach, City | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 | Confirmed (directive) / Inference (operator behaviour) | impact:watch 2️⃣ STILL TRUE — KENYA IS STILL LEVEL 2 No advisory movement on any of the five markets today. Kenya remains US Level 2 (re-issued 28 July 2026, verified 12 August); Diani, Watamu and the Nairobi hotel corridors sit outside every Level 4 zone. The UK still advises against travel to no part of Uganda (verified vs gov.uk, 28 August 2026). 🎯 So what: An agent asking about "the Kenya situation" is asking about a labour dispute that ended yesterday, not a risk level. Don't discount into a question you can answer with a link. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 | Confirmed | impact:demand 3️⃣ COST PULSE — THE FUEL CYCLE TURNS IN 13 DAYS Kenyan diesel holds at KSh 217.86/L to 14 September 2026, roughly KSh 14 above what landed costs implied, because diesel users are cross-subsidising petrol (EPRA notice / Business Daily, 14 August 2026). Diarise two dates: the EPRA review on 14 September, and the expiry of the 8% VAT rate on petroleum on 14 October 2026. 🎯 So what: Refuse any supplier fuel surcharge before 14 September — the landed-cost figure kills the argument. Model a step-up for Q4 transfers. 🏷 Bush, City | 🇰🇪 | Confirmed | impact:margin 💬 Open your own website tonight. How many green claims could you evidence in writing by 27 September? 🔗 This edition on the web: 💼 Today's Big Read on LinkedIn: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Evening Wrap · Tue 1 Sep 📌 "ECO-LODGE" STOPS BEING FREE IN 26 DAYS From 27 Sep the EU bans vague green claims — "eco", "sustainable", "carbon neutral" — unless certified. It binds you if you sell to European guests, wherever you sit. → Do this: Search your site for those words. Evidence each one, replace it with a measured fact, or delete it. 📌 ALSO TODAY 🇰🇪 No advisory movement — Kenya still US Level 2; last week's JKIA dispute ended yesterday 🇰🇪 Diesel KSh 217.86/L to 14 Sep; the 8% fuel VAT expires 14 Oct 🇺🇬 UK still advises against travel to no part of Uganda 📊 NUMBER OF THE DAY Under 3.4% — the share

records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 📅 Monday, 31 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 JKIA is delayed, not closed — and that distinction is worth money to you today. 1️⃣ JKIA STRIKE ENTERS DAY TWO. 30% OF KQ FLIGHTS LEFT BY 2PM. Kenya Aviation Workers Union members downed tools at the Kenya Airports Authority, KCAA and Jambojet on Sunday 30 August. Kenya Airways reported that only 30% of its scheduled flights had departed by 14:00 EAT , with those that went averaging two-to-three-hour delays and later departures running beyond three (KQ customer update via KATA, 30 August). Disruption continued into this morning. KAA confirms delays but reports no closure — flights are operating. 🎯 So what: Your exposure is missed onward connections , not cancellations. Any guest landing at JKIA today with a same-day Wilson or coastal leg to the Mara, Kilimanjaro or Zanzibar should be treated as at risk. Hold their room rather than releasing it, ring the DMC before the guest rings you, and offer the date change before anyone asks for a refund. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | Kenya | Confirmed | impact:risk 2️⃣ THIS IS THE THIRD ROUND OF THE SAME DISPUTE SINCE FEBRUARY. Treat this as a pattern, not an accident. The same CBA dispute shut JKIA for two days on 16–17 February 2026 — Jambojet flew just 25% of its schedule, cancelled over 40 flights and disrupted 5,000+ passengers (Jambojet CEO Karanja Ndegwa, Capital FM, 19 February). A second round was enjoined by the High Court on 23 July and suspended on 27 July under a return-to-work deal. KAWU has now lifted that suspension, saying the agencies never honoured it. 🎯 So what: February's round ended on day two via mediation led by Transport CS Davis Chirchir. That is the base rate to plan against — expect resolution in days, not weeks, and don't panic-discount Q4. But stop treating JKIA reliability as a given when you build September–December itineraries: build a buffer night in Nairobi into long-haul arrivals rather than selling same-day bush connections. 🏷 City, Bush | Kenya | Confirmed | impact:watch 3️⃣ STILL TRUE — KENYA IS STILL LEVEL 2. THIS IS NOT A RISK EVENT. We checked travel.state.gov this morning: Kenya remains Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, date issued 28 July 2026 — unchanged. No government has moved on Kenya because of the strike. 🎯 So what: When an agent asks whether Kenya is "having problems", answer precisely. A labour delay at an airport is an operations event; nothing about the country's risk posture has changed. Properties that blur the two hand a booking to the one that doesn't. 🏷 City, Bush, Beach | Kenya | Confirmed | impact:demand 📡 RADAR • KNBS August CPI due on its end-of-month pattern — July printed 6.5% (KNBS, July 2026) • Kwita Izina, Kinigi — ceremony 4 September; exhibition runs 28 Aug–8 Sep (RDB) • Miss Tourism East Africa finals, Kampala — 5–12 September • Uganda Airlines starts daily Entebbe–Kigali 18 November, Accra 27 October (announced 5 August) 💬 If a guest misses a Mara connection today, who eats the cost at your property — you, the DMC or the airline? Worth knowing before lunchtime. 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Morning Brief · Mon 31 Aug 🚨 JKIA STRIKE RUNS INTO DAY TWO Aviation workers downed tools Sunday. records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Sunday Foresight 📅 Monday, 31 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 This week's results all say the same thing: bigger top line, worse unit economics. That is the region's shape. Kenya's 2025 tourism report gave record arrivals and earnings while earnings per arrival rose 3.13% against its own 4.075% inflation assumption: real yield per guest fell. Mainland Tanzania has overtaken Zanzibar on spend per night. Now the supply table. W Hospitality Group's 2026 Africa pipeline report (10 Mar 2026): Kenya has 6,190 pipeline rooms, of which 4,922 — 79.5% — are already under construction. Ethiopia 79.9%, Tanzania 77.5%. Egypt, the continent's largest pipeline, 51.4%; Nigeria 39.2%; Cape Verde 8.6%. What everyone is missing: the trade read that table as confidence. It is the opposite. A room in planning is an option you can let expire; a room under construction is a commitment with a drawdown schedule. Egypt can defer 22,362 rooms, Nigeria 5,152, Cape Verde 3,954. Kenya can defer 1,268. When demand softens, other African markets adjust through supply. East Africa can only adjust through price — and it lands on you, not the developer. A new branded hotel opens with debt to service and no legacy rate to protect. records.title: Four things nobody has reported.
records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Special Report, Tuesday 25 August 2026 📕 SPECIAL — WE READ KENYA'S 2025 TOURISM REPORT LINE BY LINE. PART 1 OF 3: THE HEADLINE ISN'T THE STORY. The Tourism Research Institute's Annual Tourism Sector Performance Report 2025 (90pp, v8, dated 4 June 2026) is public. The press reported it in April. Almost every number in circulation is wrong. What the document actually says: international arrivals 2,652,540 in 2025, from 2,474,551 in 2024 — +7.2% . Earnings KSh 501.34bn , from KSh 453.50bn — +10.55% . What the press reported: "7.9 million visitors" · "2.7 million, +9%" · "2.55 million, +6.2%" · "Africa 47% of arrivals". None of those match the report. Africa is 37.59% (997,188). The 7.9m figure adds domestic bed-nights to international arrivals — a bed-night is not a visitor. Four things nobody has reported. 1️⃣ A tenth of your "international" arrivals are Kenyans coming home. The report states plainly that the 2,652,540 "includes 250,603 Kenyan diaspora arrivals" (p.22). That is 9.45% of the headline. Strip it out and genuine foreign arrivals are 2,401,937 , growing 6.6% , not 7.2%. Diaspora itself grew 13.4% — faster than the market. 2️⃣ Kenya grew slower than Africa. The same report cites UN Tourism: Africa +8% in 2025 (81m), the world +4%. Kenya's +7.2% sits below the continental average , and far below Egypt (+20%) and Morocco (+14%). The report never makes this comparison. 3️⃣ Real yield per arrival went backwards. Earnings ÷ arrivals: KSh 177,074 (2023) → 183,264 (2024) → 189,004 (2025) . That is +3.13% nominal. The report's own inflation assumption for 2025 is 4.075% . Real revenue per visitor fell about 0.9% . Kenya sold more nights for less real money. 4️⃣ The growth is decelerating hard. Earnings: +41.26% (2023) → +20.13% (2024) → +10.55% (2025). Arrivals: +15.71% (2024) → +7.19% (2025). Growth halved in a year. "Consolidation" is the report's word for it. 🎯 So what — this week: • Reprice off 2,401,937, not 2.7m or 7.9m. If a lender, landlord or JV partner is modelling on the inflated figure, your projected share of market is overstated by up to 3x. • Diaspora is your most defensible segment — 250,603 people, +13.4%, travelling Christmas and Easter, staying longer, spending locally. Almost nobody prices for them. Build a diaspora rate with a long-stay fence and a family-room bias before December. • Stop selling volume. With real yield falling, another 7% of arrivals at flat real rate is a busier hotel earning the same money. Coming in this series: Part 2 — the MICE numbers, and what 998 "international conferences" actually contained. Part 3 — the park-gate admission, the receivership line, and why the 2030 forecast is a straight line. 📄 Source: Tourism Research Institute, Annual Tourism Sector Performance Report 2025 , v8 dated 4 June 2026. All figures quoted are the report's own. 🔗 Full analysis on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 📕 SPECIAL (1/3): KENYA'S TOURISM NUMBERS DON'T SAY WHAT THE PRESS SAID We read the TRI Annual Report 2025 in full. Arrivals were 2,652,540 (+7.2%) , not 7.9m or 2.7m. And 250,603 of them are Kenyan diaspora — 9.45% of the headline. True foreign arrivals: 2,401,937 . Worse: earnings per arrival rose 3.13% against 4.075% inflation. Real yield fell . → Do this: Rebuild your market-share model on 2.40m, not 7.9m. And build a diaspora rate — that segment grew 13.4% and nobody prices for it. 📌 ALSO IN THE REPORT 🇰🇪 Kenya's +7.2% trailed Africa's +8% — the report never says so 🇰🇪 Growth halved: earnings +20.13% in 2024 → +10.55% in 2025 📊 NUMBER OF THE DAY: 250,603 — Kenyans in the "international arrivals" figure. 📲 Telegram: 📖 Read on the web → Kenya's Tourism Research Institute published its Annual Tourism Sector Performance Report for 2025. We read all 90 pages. The figures in circulation do not match the document. The report records 2,652,540 international arrivals, up 7.2%, and earnings of KSh 501.34 billion, up 10.55%

records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Midday Pulse, Tuesday 25 August 2026 1️⃣ 🇰🇪 ⚖️ A COURT SUSPENDED KENYA'S US$50,000 TOURIST INSURANCE RULE ON 21 AUGUST — THE TRADE ONLY NOTICED YESTERDAY The High Court at Marsabit issued conservatory orders on 21 August 2026 halting Gazette Notice No. 11492 , the travel-health insurance rule gazetted by Health CS Aden Duale on 30 July. Justice Francis Rayola Olel certified it urgent; heard inter partes 16 September 2026 (Kahawatungu / The Standard, 24–25 Aug 2026). Petitioners argue entry conditions belong to Interior and Immigration, not Health; that it encroaches on the IRA; and that uploading health data via the eTA breaches Article 31 privacy. It is the second case filed — a COFEK challenge runs alongside. Correction, ours: on 24 Aug we called this "under challenge, mention 29 Sep". It had been suspended three days earlier; 29 Sep belongs to the other case. Tracker fixed. 🎯 So what: that cost line is judicially frozen, not dormant. Quote high-season packages without it, but do not delete the clause from 2027 contracts — 16 Sep can restore it. 🏷 All · KE · Confirmed 2️⃣ 🇰🇪 ✈️ NINETY DEAD AIRCRAFT ARE DIVERTING FLIGHTS AT WILSON — YOUR SAFARI FEEDER HUB An Auditor-General audit finds 90 grounded aircraft occupying apron space at Wilson, "forcing flight diversions" and costing KAA revenue (Nancy Gathungu, via Business Daily, 23 Aug 2026). Wilson handled 83,855 movements in the year to June 2025 vs 65,512 in 2021 — up 28%. About five aircraft have been auctioned since 2024, when the count was 70; it is now 90. Some traffic is pushed to Orly Airpark near Kiserian. The audit also flags no proper terminal — a corridor holding 50 passengers — and incomplete screening. On 24 Aug KCAA acting DG Nicholas Bondo said training schools should move off Wilson, with landing and parking charges under discussion (People Daily, 24 Aug 2026). Read the mechanism correctly: the constraint is apron parking , not runway slots — and flight schools are not the dead metal. records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Evening Wrap, Sunday 23 August 2026 🌍 THE EXPERT BRIEF — TANZANIA IS NOW POWER-LONG. ZANZIBAR STILL CAN'T PLUG IN. On 22 August Tanzania inaugurated the 2,115MW Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project, lifting installed capacity to 4,646MW against roughly 2,271MW of peak demand — a surplus near 2,375MW (TanzaniaInvest, 23 Aug 2026). For a region where hotels budget diesel gensets as a standing cost line, a neighbour turning structurally power-long is a competitiveness event. The catch most will miss: the surplus stops at the water. Zanzibar — Tanzania's highest-value tourism zone — draws power over two submarine cables running at 98.8% and 97.3% of capacity, capping reliable island supply near 135MW against a ~65MW deficit (The Citizen TZ / AfDB). The bottleneck has moved from generation to transmission. Mainland abundance does not reach an Unguja beach resort until the planned 220kV upgrade and new 270MW cable are commissioned. 🎯 So what, by segment: • CITY (Dar, Arusha, Dodoma): the clear winner — grid reliability should ease genset reliance. Revisit 2027 diesel-backup assumptions, but don't bank a tariff cut nobody has announced. • BUSH: mostly off-grid solar+diesel, so direct gain is marginal; the win is gateway-town reliability and cold chain. • BEACH (Zanzibar): do NOT cut genset capex or fuel budgets on the mainland headline — your power risk is unchanged this season. • KE BENCHMARK: Kenya's EPRA pass-through charges hit a combined KSh4.70/kWh in August (Kenyans.co.ke, 18 Aug 2026), on Nairobi diesel at KSh217.86/L. records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Sunday Foresight 📅 Sunday, 23 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇹🇿 🇷🇼 Four stories this week. One argument underneath. THE TOURIST SHILLING IS BEING RE-NATIONALISED On 18 August the Zanzibar Commission for Tourism, with Immigration, arrested three people for running excursions. The offence was nationality: under the Tourism Act 2009 tour operating and boat businesses are reserved for Zanzibaris, and a Kenyan and two Ugandans are, in law, foreigners (The Citizen, 21–22 Aug) — awkwardly against the EAC Common Market Protocol, as the reporting notes. Alone, a compliance story. Beside the week, something larger. Nairobi wants the Tourism Fund to keep collecting the 2% hotel levy while the CS oversees spending (Capital FM, 21 Aug). Dodoma is handing TANAPA and Ngorongoro back 51% of collected revenue (Pindi Chana, May 2026). Kigali prices a gorilla at US$1,500 on the wrong passport, about US$200 on an EAC one (RDB, 2026). None generates a visitor. Each redistributes money that already exists. What everyone is missing: the perimeter is drawn at the national border, not the EAC one — exactly where the growth guest now comes from. Kenyan residents were 45% of hotel occupancy in 2025 (KNBS, Apr 2026); Uganda sent Kenya 234,556 arrivals. And your growth is migrating out of room revenue into the experience layer — permits, gates, transfers, excursions — which is the layer being nationalised. Where your margin now sits, the state is not just your tax collector but your licensor. THE WEEK'S SIGNALS 1️⃣ ZANZIBAR ARRESTS EAC CITIZENS AS "FOREIGNERS" One Kenyan, two Ugandans, detained 18 Aug for excursion work reserved for Zanzibaris (The Citizen, 21–22 Aug). 🎯 So what: audit every excursion, transfer and boat product you sell or subcontract for the licence holder's nationality. This decides whether your levy funds marketing you benefit from, or institutions you don't. 🏷 City/Bush/Beach | KE | Confirmed | impact:margin 3️⃣ TANZANIA HANDS THE PARKS BACK 51% OF THE GATE Retained in Bank of Tanzania special accounts, released with Paymaster General approval (Pindi Chana, May 2026). 🎯 So what: a park funding its own roads has the motive to reprice them. Model an increase into 2027/28 costings now. 🏷 Bush | Tanzania | Confirmed | impact:watch 4️⃣ UGANDA IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE UCAA reviewed 15 air service licence applications — 10 new — on 12 June 2026; Entebbe handled 189,130 international passengers in April. 🎯 So what: Uganda is opening the layer everyone else closes. records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Evening Wrap, Saturday 22 August 2026 🌆 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 🗓 Saturday 22 August 2026 | 🇺🇬 🇷🇼 Seventy thousand Ebola vaccine doses reached the DRC this week. They read like the cavalry. They are not — and Uganda's tourism trough is longer than the headline suggests. 1️⃣ 🇨🇩➡️🇺🇬 THE EBOLA VACCINE THAT WON'T LIFT UGANDA'S "DO NOT TRAVEL" The UN's vaccine coordination group allocated 70,000 Ervebo doses to the DRC this week — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial, 50,000 for frontline health workers (WHO & Africa CDC, 20 Aug). The catch operators need to hold: Ervebo is a Zaire-strain vaccine, and its efficacy against the Bundibugyo virus driving this outbreak is unproven — that is what the trial exists to test. So this is a research event, not a containment event. The DRC epidemic is still the fastest-growing on record — 5,290 cases, 2,516 deaths to 19 Aug, up 81 cases in a day, with an M23 conflict blocking the contact-tracing containment depends on (ECDC, 21 Aug). 🏷 Bush · Uganda/Rwanda · Confirmed (WHO/Africa CDC 20 Aug; ECDC 21 Aug) 🎯 So what: The reflex read — "vaccines arriving → outbreak turning → advisory relief coming" — is wrong. A trial gives the US State Department no basis to move Uganda off Level 4 or Rwanda off Level 3 . Uganda closed its own 20-case flare-up weeks ago; it carries the advisory for its neighbour's crisis, not its own. Plan the Ugandan gorilla-tourism trough as a long tail into 2027 , not a Q4 rebound — and lean on regional and non-US source markets while the US sits at "Do Not Travel". 2️⃣ 🇺🇸 US COURT VOIDS THE 75-COUNTRY VISA BAN — READ THE SMALL PRINT A federal judge (Jeannette Vargas, SDNY) struck down the Trump administration's suspension of immigrant visas to nationals of 75 countries as beyond the Secretary of State's authority (Al Jazeera / CNN, 22 Aug). 🏷 All · Source markets · Confirmed (22 Aug) 🎯 So what: It covers immigrant (permanent-residence) visas only — not tourist or student visas — so there is no direct inbound-leisure effect. Relevance is diaspora/VFR traffic and a reminder that US entry policy remains a moving target. Don't let an agent read this as "the US just reopened travel." ✅ STILL TRUE — No EA advisory moved today (radar logged only a Lebanon change). Kenya US Level 2 ; Uganda Level 4 (DRC-Ebola grounds); Tanzania & Zanzibar Level 3 ; Rwanda Level 3 . The DRC was the single largest source market — 185,420 visitors, 12.5% of arrivals — ahead of Kenya's 148,320 (Rwanda NISR H1 2026). Not the UK, not the US. The demand is cross-border trade, healthcare, education, family, and Kigali's pull as a conference hub. The airlines see it. Uganda Airlines flies Entebbe–Kigali daily from 18 Nov and Entebbe–Accra 4x weekly from 27 Oct (announced 5 Aug, The EastAfrican). Behind it: the US$2.6bn Qatar-backed Bugesera airport , built for regional and connecting volume (operational 2028). Seats are re-basing toward intra-African traffic in real time. What everyone is missing: the regional African guest now topping the table behaves nothing like the European bucket-lister most EA properties price for. They book later, stay shorter, travel midweek for business and family, and anchor to regional — not European — price norms. Run long-haul rate fences, seven-night minimums and wholesale packaging against them and you leak occupancy AND rate without seeing why. 🎯 So what: • City: your growth guest. Build a real midweek regional-corporate rate, shorten minimum stays, cut booking and payment friction. Kigali — the DRC is now your No.1 feeder. • Bush: don't hard-code the card to the European rate. Hold a regional shoulder product; sell tight 1–2 night park add-ons off the new daily Kampala–Kigali link. • Beach: feeder-hub capacity (Nairobi, Kigali, Addis, Doha) matters more than any single European route. 2️⃣ ✈️ RWANDAIR TRIMS A BRUSSELS FREQUENCY FOR WINTER The filing removes the Monday rotation on the Kigali–Paris CDG–Brussels route for NW26; Paris stays bookable (AeroRoutes, 20 Aug). records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Evening Wrap, Friday 21 August 2026 🌆 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 🗓 Friday 21 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇹🇿 Two governments moved on the tourism value chain today — Kenya over who controls its research, finance and levy money; Zanzibar over who is allowed to run the excursions. 1️⃣ 🇰🇪 MPs MOVE AGAINST THE KTB SUPER-MERGER — AND THE MINISTRY REACHES FOR THE LEVY The Tourism (Amendment) Bill 2026 — which folds the Tourism Research Institute (TRI) and Tourism Finance Corporation (TFC) into the Kenya Tourism Board — hit resistance in committee today. The National Assembly's Tourism & Wildlife Committee (chair Kareke Mbiuki) opposed absorbing TRI, with coastal MPs (Kisauni, Lamu East, Voi) arguing it should be funded, not merged (Capital FM, 21 Aug). Separately, the Ministry of Tourism proposed splitting collection of the 2% Tourism Fund levy from management of the fund , expanding the Cabinet Secretary's oversight (allAfrica / Capital FM, 21 Aug). 🏷 City/Bush/Beach · Kenya · Confirmed (Capital FM / allAfrica, 21 Aug) 🎯 So what: TRI is the source of the arrivals-by-market and bed-night numbers you use to forecast yield and build DMC packages — losing its independence, or its funding, degrades the data you price on. And a levy whose collection and disbursement rules are being redrawn is a cash-flow and marketing-spend variable : Tourism Fund money underwrites destination and MICE marketing. Track the Bill's committee stage; don't assume either the merger or the levy mechanics land as first drafted. 2️⃣ 🇹🇿 ZANZIBAR ARRESTS THREE FOREIGNERS FOR RUNNING EXCURSIONS RESERVED FOR ZANZIBARIS The Zanzibar Commission for Tourism and Immigration arrested three foreign nationals — including Kenyan businesswoman Esther Mutheu Samuka (with Mukembo Emmanuel and Karungi Scovia) — on 18 August for operating tour and excursion businesses reserved for Zanzibari citizens under the Tourism Act No. 6 of 2009 . A public notice was issued 17 Aug (Citizen Digital / Kenyans.co.ke, 21 Aug). 🏷 Beach · Zanzibar · Confirmed (ZCT notice 17 Aug / press 21 Aug) 🎯 So what: The ground product on Zanzibar — excursions, spice tours, transfers — is legally reserved for locals. A regional DMC selling Zanzibar packages must run those legs through a licensed Zanzibari operator , not a foreign-owned entity, or risk arrest, a stranded guest and transfer liability mid-stay. Audit your island partners' licensing before the European peak, not during it. ✅ STILL TRUE — No EA advisory moved today. records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Midday Pulse, Thursday 20 August 2026 🕛 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Midday Pulse 🗓 Thursday 20 August 2026 | 🇺🇬 🇷🇼 🌍 DRC's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has passed 5,000 cases and 2,378 deaths, and WHO's emergency committee reconvened on 18 August — the reason Uganda sits at US Level 4 and Rwanda at Level 3, both unchanged. 1️⃣ 🌍 DRC EBOLA PASSES 5,000 CASES — WHO EMERGENCY COMMITTEE RECONVENES 18 AUG WHO AFRO's 18 August report puts the DRC Bundibugyo outbreak at 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths (data to 16 Aug), across 55 health zones in six provinces — up from 4,318 cases / 2,011 deaths on 9 August. It is the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC's history and the fastest-growing on record. Ituri stays the epicentre (4,257 cases, 1,878 deaths). The point that matters for us is the eastward creep : North Kivu now 607 cases / 428 deaths across 12 of 34 zones, and South Kivu recording its first cases (3 cases, 1 death). Both provinces border Uganda and Rwanda. WHO's IHR Emergency Committee — first convened 22 May, when the outbreak was declared a PHEIC — met again on 18 August (WHO, 18 Aug). records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Morning Brief, Tuesday 19 August 2026 ☀️ MORNING BRIEF — Tue 19 Aug 2026 Quiet news slot — one expert read that matters more than any headline. Worse, the same treasuries celebrating this demand are taxing its most price-sensitive flyer. Kenya's JKIA passenger levy is now pledged to bondholders (Business Daily, 24 Jul) — hard to cut — with a 2% short-term-rental levy and a proposed travel-health-insurance charge stacking on top. records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Evening Wrap, Wednesday 19 August 2026 🌙 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 🗓 Wednesday 19 August 2026 | 🇺🇬 The Big Read Expert Brief: the smart money is building in Uganda — while its most valuable long-haul market is told "Do Not Travel." 🇺🇬 UGANDA'S HOTEL BRANDS ARE BUILDING THROUGH A LEVEL-4 TROUGH Read the openings and Uganda looks like a market on the way up. Marriott put its flagship brand into Kampala for the first time this year — a 277-unit twin-tower on Nsambya Hill, opened June 2026 (The Independent UG, 11 Aug). Asilia enters the country with Erebero Hills , an eight-suite gorilla lodge on the edge of Bwindi, opening this season (Travel Weekly, 2026). And the region's investor circuit — Future Hospitality Summit Africa — has awarded Kampala its 2027 edition at Speke Resort (Breaking Travel News). Uganda sits at US State Department Level 4 — Do Not Travel , raised on Ebola grounds (travel.state.gov, via advisory board verified 12 Aug), with a US inbound restriction for anyone in Uganda in the prior 21 days. The Level 4 is pinned to the DRC epidemic next door — now ~5,000 cases, 2,300+ deaths, the fastest-growing on record (WHO IHR committee, 18 Aug). records.text: 📊 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Special Edition 🗓 Tuesday 18 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 KNBS data drop Kenya's arrivals are up — but not where the headline says. Mombasa's Moi International (MIA) took 96,701 arrivals, up 19.7% year-on-year, while JKIA grew 8.5% and land borders 7.5% . The coast is recovering over twice as fast as the Nairobi gateway. What everyone is missing: the +9.5% is not evenly yours. In April — the long-rains trough — national arrivals rose just 2.9% and JKIA fell 1.0% YoY. Strip the coast out and the city-gateway recovery is modest and seasonal. A Nairobi GM reading "+9.5%" as their own demand is reading the wrong line. Backing it: SGR passengers ran ~12% ahead in Q1 — the Nairobi–Mombasa corridor is carrying this (KNBS). 🏷 City/Beach · Kenya · Confirmed (KNBS arrivals & SGR) / Inference (regional read) 🎯 So what: Coast — demand is arriving; hold rate through the Sep–Oct build and stop discounting. records.text: 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 🗓 Tuesday 18 August 2026 | 🌍 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇷🇼 🇹🇿 Expert Brief: East Africa is adding air routes faster than its airlines can afford to fly them. 1️⃣ 🌍 THE AIRLIFT YOU'RE CELEBRATING IS THE LEAST PROFITABLE IN THE WORLD Every route launch lands as good news in this business. Uganda Airlines opens Entebbe–Accra on 27 Oct and daily Entebbe–Kigali on 18 Nov (announced 5 Aug, The EastAfrican); Airlink starts Cape Town–Zanzibar on 3 Oct. Read the balance sheet underneath and the mood changes. IATA's December outlook put African carriers at US$1.30 of profit per passenger for 2026 against a US$7.90 global average — a 1.3% margin, the thinnest of any region (IATA, 9 Dec 2025). By its June AGM it had cut the 2026 line again: profit per passenger down to 40 US cents from US$2.10 in 2025, and the continent's total net profit halved to ~US$100m (IATA "Energy in Crisis" outlook, 8 Jun 2026). East Africa's recovery is riding on the most fragile airlift economics on the planet. What everyone is missing: a new-route press release reads as demand arriving. It is actually thin-margin capacity being lent — and thin-margin capacity is the first thing cut when a season underperforms. Turkish suspended 18 routes for summer 2026, Istanbul–Dar es Salaam among them, final flights in May/June (reported 2026). The route you don't help fill in its first two seasons is the route that isn't there in year three. Airlift is not infrastructure you inherit; it's a trade relationship you keep alive. 🏷 City/Bush/Beach · Regional · Confirmed (IATA figures & schedules) / Inference (fragility read) 🎯 So what — by segment: City (Nairobi/Kigali/Kampala): put corporate blocks and MICE contracts onto the new regional frequencies so they survive to a third season. Bush: the luxury pivot means fewer, higher-value guests who still need a long-haul seat — cultivate the carriers that actually serve your source markets. Beach: feeder routes are the most fragile of all — a trial like Cape Town–Zanzibar lives or dies on load factor. Fill it or lose it. ✅ STILL TRUE — Tanzania & Zanzibar remain US Level 3 (unchanged since 31 Oct 2025); Kenya Level 2 , core tourist corridors clear (travel.state.gov, verified 12 Aug). records.text: 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 🗓 Sunday 16 August 2026 | 🇹🇿 🇰🇪 🇷🇼 Zanzibar just posted its best July on record. The number that should worry you is May's. 1️⃣ 🇹🇿 ZANZIBAR'S RECORD JULY WIDENED THE GAP IT SHOULD HAVE CLOSED 107,801 visitors in July — an all-time monthly record, +9.6% on July 2025's 98,370 (OCGS, via The Citizen, 14 Aug). It was also +54.9% on June's 69,605, and 2.68× May's 40,151 . A year earlier that same step was +45.7%. The swing didn't narrow. It widened by nine points. The Maldives, on months published so far in 2026, ran 247,722 in February to 123,552 in June — 2.01× (Maldives Monetary Authority). Definitions differ, but the direction isn't in doubt: Zanzibar is getting better at selling ten weeks and no better at selling the other forty-two. What everyone is missing: the record was disproportionately not European. Europe supplied 60,754, yet its share fell from 61.9% in June to 56.4% in July. Back out the residual and non-European arrivals grew +77.5% month-on-month, against Europe's +40.9%. The marginal guest is increasingly African, Gulf and Asian — booking shorter, later, outside European tour-operator rails. That is the only demand that doesn't obey a European school calendar, and the only demand that can flatten this curve. 🏷 Beach · Tanzania/Zanzibar · Confirmed (OCGS & MMA figures) / Inference (amplitude read) 🎯 So what: Price April–May as an unbuilt product, not a failed season. Reported as a leisure route. Read it as a seasonality instrument: year-round regional airlift from a market whose holiday calendar doesn't track Europe's. One rotation won't flatten a 2.68× curve — but it's the shape of the thing that does. 🏷 Beach · Tanzania/South Africa · Confirmed (schedule) / Inference (read) 🎯 So what: If you sell Zanzibar, get South African trade and Cape Town connecting traffic onto your rate sheet before October. ✅ STILL TRUE — Tanzania and Zanzibar remain US Level 3 , unchanged since 31 Oct 2025 (travel.state.gov, verified 4 Aug 2026); the UK has no advisory against travel to Zanzibar. records.title: 1️⃣ 🇺🇬 washington already writes uganda in the past tense — and keeps it restricted anyway
records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Midday Pulse 🗓 Sunday 16 August 2026 | 🇺🇬 🇰🇪 🌍 The order that keeps Uganda restricted was filed on Friday and publishes tomorrow. We've read it. Uganda's 28 August all-clear is not what releases it. 1️⃣ 🇺🇬 WASHINGTON ALREADY WRITES UGANDA IN THE PAST TENSE — AND KEEPS IT RESTRICTED ANYWAY The full text of the US entry order signed on 12 August went on public inspection at the Federal Register on 14 August, 08:45 and publishes 17 August (FR Doc 2026-16706 , docket CDC-2026-0892 ). We read it this morning on public inspection; we haven't seen it reported anywhere yet. Two things in it matter more than the renewal we covered on 13 August. First, the operative finding. The determination reads that Ebola is "confirmed currently present in DRC and recently present in Uganda ." Past tense — in a document that keeps Uganda on the restricted list. The order records Uganda's last confirmed case as 21 June , 20 confirmed cases and two deaths in total, and the Ministry of Health declaration of 28 July . It then keeps Uganda in on a stated ground that has nothing to do with Uganda's epidemiology: "continued overland travel from DRC poses an ongoing risk of cross-border transmission, particularly among healthcare workers and in western Ugandan districts." What everyone is missing: the release condition is a DRC number, not a Ugandan one. The order names contact tracing at ~78% nationwide against a 95% operational threshold , says the true outbreak size may be "two to four times greater" than reported, and puts DRC at 4,318 confirmed cases and 2,011 deaths across 53 health zones as of 9 August — against 1,873 and 672 across 41 zones when the July order was signed. Uganda's 42-day clock completing around 28 August does not move any of those. Expiry is 4:59pm EDT, Friday 11 September . Second, there is a door, and nobody has walked through it. Publication on 17 August opens a 15-day comment period on docket CDC-2026-0892 — closing on or about 1 September , ahead of the 11 September call. The order records the comments received so far: three on the original, five in June, and on the July renewal, none . The East African trade has never filed. 🏷 Uganda/Regional · Bush/City · Confirmed (FR Doc 2026-16706, public inspection 14 Aug) / Inference (release-condition read) 🎯 So what: Stop selling 28 August as the turning point — brief agents that the US rule is priced to run to 11 September, and rebook US arrivals accordingly. If you want Uganda decoupled, the comment docket is the only formal channel into the risk assessment that decides it, it costs nothing, and it closes ~1 September. 2️⃣ 🌍 TWO OFFICIAL CASE COUNTS FOR THE SAME DAY — 63 APART Worth knowing before you quote a number to an agent or an insurer. For 9 August , the US order states DRC at 4,318 confirmed cases across 53 health zones . WHO AFRO's Weekly External Situation Report 13, same reporting date, states 4,381 confirmed cases and 2,011 deaths, a case fatality ratio of 45.9% , with Ituri accounting for 85.8% of cumulative cases (afro.who.int, posted 11 Aug). Deaths agree exactly. Cases differ by 63. Neither is wrong — the US figure is a snapshot taken for an American risk assessment; WHO AFRO's is the regional surveillance line. But they will be quoted against each other in the coming fortnight, and being caught with the lower one looks like minimising. 🏷 Regional · Bush/City · Confirmed (both documents, dated) 🎯 So what: Standardise on WHO AFRO for any client-facing figure, cite it with the report number and date, and never quote an outbreak number without one. ✅ STILL TRUE — The order leaves the CDC travel health notice for all of Uganda at Level 2 (practice enhanced precautions), with Level 4 confined to Ituri and North Kivu in DRC (escalated 4 Aug) and Level 3 to South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo. records.text: 🌙 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Evening Wrap 🗓 Sunday 16 August 2026 | 🌍 🇺🇬 🇰🇪 Africa's own scientists have put a number on the outbreak that decides Uganda's US restriction. It went the wrong way — and the vaccine line is no longer supportable. 1️⃣ 🌍 THE VACCINE LINE IS NO LONGER SUPPORTABLE — AND THE RELEASE NUMBER ROSE At midday we said the condition freeing Uganda from the US entry order is a DRC number. Tonight we have it. Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group, chaired by Prof. Salim Abdool Karim, reports 4,449 confirmed cases, 2,061 deaths, 46.3% fatality in DRC, ~100 new cases a day , R(t) consistently above 1 (Africa CDC statement, 14 August ). Its words: the epidemic is "still growing rapidly, and faster than previous Ebola epidemics." Against the US order's 4,318 and WHO AFRO's 4,381 for 9 August, the curve has not turned. What everyone is missing: the vaccine sentence. On Ervebo against Bundibugyo the ECG is blunt — "no reliable evidence of its clinical efficacy" , and "a reasonable chance the vaccine is not effective." It recommends use under trial protocol , not rollout. Since 2019 the reassurance script has been "Ebola is vaccine-preventable." For this strain, Africa's own experts say that is not established. And 63% of deaths in the last fortnight occurred in the community , not treatment centres — detection, not capacity, is the constraint. 🏷 Regional · Bush/City · Confirmed (Africa CDC ECG statement, 14 Aug) / Inference (release-condition read) 🎯 So what: Strike the vaccine line from every agent script and insurer letter tonight. Use transmission facts instead — no Ugandan case since 21 June, none outside Kampala, no community spread. Brief 11 September as continuation, not release. 2️⃣ 🌍 TWO CDC PAGES, TWO DIFFERENT MAPS We checked both tonight; we haven't seen this reported anywhere. CDC's Travel Health Notices index (read 16 Aug, ~19:00 EAT) states under Level 4: "Currently there are no Travel Health Notices at this level." Its Ebola notices — Level 3 for Ituri, North and South Kivu , Level 2 for DRC and Uganda — are dated 15 June 2026 . CDC's Ebola situation summary (page dated updated 12 August 2026 ) instead "recommends avoiding all travel to Ituri and Nord-Kivu... and avoiding nonessential travel to Haut-Uele and Tshopo." Not the same map. Risk vendors and insurers ingest the index because it is machine-readable — so a client's system sees June while their risk officer reads August. 🏷 Regional · City/Bush · Confirmed (both pages, with their own dates) / Inference (vendor-ingestion read) 🎯 So what: When an account cites "CDC guidance", ask which page, dated when. Neither names Kenya, Tanzania, Zanzibar or Rwanda — lead with that. ✅ STILL TRUE — The live CDC index confirms our midday reading: Uganda at Level 2 . Tanzania and Zanzibar remain US Level 3 , unchanged since 31 Oct 2025 (travel.state.gov, verified 4 Aug). Don't discount as though something moved. ⚡ COST PULSE — Nairobi diesel holds at KSh 217.86/L to 14 Sep — ~ KSh 14.28/L above landed-cost parity (EPRA / Business Daily, 14 Aug). 📅 WEEK AHEAD — 17 Aug CDC comment window opens · 18 Aug WHO IHR Committee on the PHEIC · 18–20 Aug AfPIF, Kigali · 19–21 Aug Hotel Expo Kenya, KICC · ~28 Aug Uganda's 42-day all-clear · 28 Aug WTA Africa Gala, Zanzibar · 11 Sep CDC decision. 💬 Which CDC page does your biggest corporate account read — have you asked? 🔗 This edition on the web: 💼 Today's Big Read on LinkedIn: — EA Hospitality Pulse 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Evening Wrap · Sun 16 Aug 🚨 THE VACCINE LINE IS NO LONGER SUPPORTABLE Africa CDC's expert group (statement, 14 Aug) finds "no reliable evidence" Ervebo works against the Bundibugyo strain, and wants it used under trial protocol — not rolled out. records.text: 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Sunday Foresight 🗓 Sunday 16 August 2026 | 🇹🇿 🇰🇪 🇺🇬 🇷🇼 THE THEME: YOUR PACE REPORT ONLY SEES THE CHANNEL THAT'S SHRINKING Two numbers landed three days apart. On 14 Aug Zanzibar posted July arrivals of 107,801 — an all-time record, +9.6% year on year (OCGS via The Citizen). What everyone is missing: this is a measurement failure before it is a demand story. Pace and allocation were built on the shrinking channel and barely see the growing one, so the pace report shows a hole that isn't there — and the reflex is to discount into it. The short-window channel also cancels at double the rate: 21.8% OTA vs 10.6% direct (Cloudbeds, 25 Mar 2026). Expiry 11 Sep , comments close ~ 1 Sep . WHO AFRO put DRC at 4,381 confirmed, CFR 45.9% as of 9 Aug (SitRep 13, 11 Aug). 🎯 So what: Brief agents to 11 Sep, not 28 Aug — and file on the docket before ~1 Sep. records.text: 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 🗓 Saturday 15 August 2026 | 🇰🇪 🇷🇼 🇹🇿 Your diesel got Sh5 cheaper today. The market said it should have been Sh19.28. The gap is the story. 1️⃣ 🇰🇪 YOU GOT SH5 OFF DIESEL. THE MARKET GAVE SH19.28 EPRA's schedule takes effect today , to 14 September: Nairobi diesel Sh217.86/L (–Sh5), petrol held at Sh214.03 , kerosene Sh191.38 . But landed diesel fell 13.08% last month — US$855.59/m³ from US$984.37 — while landed petrol rose 6.9% . On the regulator's own disclosures diesel should have dropped Sh19.28, to Sh203.58 . The State used diesel to cross-subsidise petrol, plus Sh938m of stabilisation (Business Daily, 14 Aug, quoting acting EPRA DG Joseph Oketch). What everyone is missing: the Sh5 isn't relief. Diesel is the safari cost line — game drives, transfers, generators, boreholes, laundry — and operators are carrying Sh14.28/L above market so Nairobi's motorists don't feel the Iran-war spike. records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Morning Brief Thursday 13 August 2026 The United States renewed its Ebola entry order on 12 August 2026 and kept Uganda inside it — but Canada's rule is the harder one, and it expires on 29 August. Canada, by contrast, requires a 21-day quarantine on arrival for anyone who has been in Uganda or South Sudan in the previous 21 days. Most East African operators are briefing agents on "the US restrictions" as though the two are the same. They are not. --- 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Morning Brief 🗓 Thursday 13 August 2026 | 🇺🇬 🇨🇦 🇺🇸 Yesterday we said the framework was being re-decided. It was. DRC arrivals are barred outright. records.title: 1️⃣ 🇷🇼 rwanda is buying yield, not volume — and airlift is the catch
records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Midday Pulse Thursday 13 August 2026 Rwanda is buying its way up-market on two fronts at once — branded ultra-luxury beds and business-events volume — and both bets run into the same wall: airlift. In the space of a fortnight, The Lux Collective signed a five-property LUX /SALT circuit with Cleo Capital and RSSB (Africa CEO Forum, Kigali, announced 31 July 2026), and the 15th African Peering & Interconnection Forum brings 300–500 delegates to the Kigali Marriott next week (18–20 August). Both point the same way: Rwanda is chasing revenue per visitor, not visitor volume. That is the right instinct — and the thing that decides whether it works is the price of a plane seat, not the thread count. --- 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Midday Pulse 🗓 Thursday 13 August 2026 | 🇷🇼 🇿🇦 🌍 A quiet news day, so a longer look: Rwanda is doubling down on yield-per-guest. The catch is one everyone keeps forgetting. 1️⃣ 🇷🇼 RWANDA IS BUYING YIELD, NOT VOLUME — AND AIRLIFT IS THE CATCH Two signings a fortnight apart tell one story. The Lux Collective is bringing a five-property LUX /SALT circuit to Rwanda with Cleo Capital and RSSB — inked at the Africa CEO Forum in Kigali, announced 31 July 2026 . Phase one (mid-2026) rebrands Cleo Lake Kivu as LUX Lake Kivu and Akagera Game Lodge as SALT of Akagera ; phase two adds three greenfield LUX at Volcanoes, Nyungwe and Akagera for 2028 . Alongside it, the 15th AfPIF brings 300–500 delegates to the Kigali Marriott, 18–20 August — one node in an RDB MICE revenue target of US$156m for 2026 ($130m in 2025, $187m projected 2027, per RDB). Kigali has held Africa's No.2 meetings city for five straight years behind Cape Town (2024 ICCA rankings). What everyone is missing: both bets land into the same constraint — thin, expensive intra-African airlift. Rwanda issues just 112 gorilla permits a day (RDB); five new branded properties add rooms, not seats and not permits. The near-term effect of new supply is yield pressure on existing premium camps , not net new demand — more branded beds chasing a permit-capped, seat-capped market. South Africa's headline "arrivals" push is a volume play; the real rival threat isn't its visitor number, it's Southern Africa and Morocco buying long-haul lift . Lift, not brand, is the battleground. 🏷 Rwanda/Regional · Bush/City · Confirmed (deals + figures) / Inference (yield read) 🎯 So what — bush: The Lux pipeline is a 2028 supply shock into a market capped at 112 permits/day. Lock DMC allocations and rate parity for 2028 peak now , before branded supply resets the anchor. Watch construction-phase generator and utility load near Kivu, Volcanoes and Nyungwe sites. 🎯 So what — city: Hold corporate rate through AfPIF week (18–21 Aug) rather than discounting into association-conference compression — but right-size it: 300–500 delegates fills the Marriott and its near neighbours, not all of Kigali. 🎯 So what — Kenya/Tanzania: Rwanda's yield-per-guest model is the template. Sell the multi-country EA itinerary Southern Africa structurally can't match — gorillas plus savannah plus beach — because the rival fight is over airlift, and EA's answer is a bundled product, not a price war. 📅 MICE WATCH — 15th AfPIF , Kigali Marriott, 18–20 Aug (300–500 delegates, af-ix.org). One entry in Rwanda's US$156m 2026 MICE target (RDB). ✅ STILL TRUE — Rwanda gorilla permit holds at US$1,500 for foreign non-residents (RDB, 2026): the region's priciest single wildlife ticket, and the pricing anchor the new LUX supply is built around. Don't model a discount into 2028. 📅 WEEK AHEAD — EPRA Kenya fuel review ~14 Aug ; WHO IHR Emergency Committee 18 Aug ; Hotel Expo Kenya 19–21 Aug (KICC); WTA Africa Gala , Zanzibar, 28 Aug . 💬 If new branded supply lands into fixed permits and fixed seats, does it grow the market — or just re-price it? 🔗 This edition on the web: — EA Hospitality Pulse | Daily intelligence for city, bush & beach properties 🏨 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE Midday Pulse · Thu 13 Aug 📌 RWANDA

records.title: Expert Brief: The airlift East Africa is banking its 2026 arrivals on is being flown by carriers earning 40 US cents a passenger. Read the balance sheet behind the route map, not just the route map.
records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Morning Brief Tuesday 11 August 2026 Expert Brief: The airlift East Africa is banking its 2026 arrivals on is being flown by carriers earning 40 US cents a passenger. Read the balance sheet behind the route map, not just the route map. --- 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Tue 11 Aug, Morning Quiet news morning. One Expert Brief, then the board. 1️⃣ THE ROUTE MAP LOOKS LIKE GROWTH. THE MARGIN BEHIND IT LOOKS LIKE FRAGILITY. Every new frequency into Nairobi, Entebbe, Kigali and Zanzibar reads to an owner as free demand. More seats, more guests, plan the rooms around them. That is the wrong thing to be watching. The carriers flying those seats are the least profitable in the world. IATA's outlook (December 2025, revised down through 2026) puts African airlines' 2026 net profit at about US$100m — a 0.2% margin, and roughly US$0.40 per passenger, down from US$2.10 in 2025 . Africa is simultaneously the fastest-growing aviation market on earth (demand up ~10%) and the thinnest-margin one, carrying the highest unit costs globally — near 140 US-cents per ATK, about double the industry average (IATA/AFRAA). What everyone is missing: a route launch is not a demand guarantee — it's a bet made by an operator with no buffer. At a 0.2% margin, the first thing a carrier trims when fuel, FX or bookings wobble is the newest, thinnest route. And those are precisely the frequencies feeding secondary safari and beach gateways. Airlift you didn't build, you can't defend. 🎯 So what, by segment 🦁 Bush: most exposed. A safari season hung on one newly launched or seasonal regional frequency is a fragile plan — keep multi-gateway routing and push direct/advance bookings so a schedule cut doesn't empty your season. 🏖 Beach: single-carrier leisure and charter routes (e.g. RwandAir's Zanzibar/Mombasa services resumed Dec 2025) are the classic first-to-be-trimmed in a squeeze. Hold rate, but keep a source-market and routing spread. 🏙 City: trunk routes on the strongest balance sheets are your safest airlift — but don't bank every new frequency straight into corporate-rate assumptions. 🏷 Regional · All segments · Confidence: High (figures dated & sourced) --- 📋 THE BOARD ✅ STILL TRUE — Uganda US Level 4 "Do Not Travel" unchanged (State Dept, 5 Aug); Kenya Level 2 ; TZ & Zanzibar Level 3 . The Uganda/DRC decoupling question resolves tomorrow, not today — don't price a US-market rebound you can't yet see. 📅 WEEK AHEAD — US CDC Section 362 entry order lapses or renews ~12 Aug (4:59pm EDT decision point); EPRA Kenya fuel review ~14 Aug (petrol held KSh214.03/L, diesel KSh222.86/L to 14 Aug, EPRA Jul review), new schedule effective 15 Aug; Hotel Expo Kenya 19–21 Aug (KICC). 🎤 MICE WATCH — Hotel Expo Kenya, Nairobi/KICC, 19–21 Aug (city midweek bump). WTA Africa Gala, Zanzibar, 28 Aug (north/east coast compression, last week of Aug). 📡 RADAR — Upstream source poll returned nothing new in-window this slot; edition built from a manual upstream scan (advisories, WHO/Africa CDC, IATA/AFRAA, EPRA). Advisory board and outbreak status unchanged since the weekend. No exclusive to report. 🔗 This edition on the web: --- 📌 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Tue 11 Aug Read the balance sheet behind the route map, not just the route map. Tonight's Big Read: reading the Amboseli elephant deaths as an operator, then the board. 🐘 THE BIG READ — A REPUTATIONAL TEST, NOT A BOOKING THREAT Kenya Wildlife Service is running a multi-agency probe into 16 elephants that died across the Amboseli–Kimana–Kitenden ecosystem between 24 June and 31 July . Preliminary University of Nairobi toxicology points to cyanide poisoning ; KWS and the Pest Control Products Board are examining whether agricultural chemicals were misused or dumped near the park edge. Confirmatory tests are pending. Amboseli remains fully operational. (People Daily / Xinhua, ~7 Aug.) Read it correctly. This is not a poaching resurgence, a disease event, or any risk to visitors — the likely pathway is agrochemical poisoning where farmland now presses against the park's wildlife dispersal corridors. Your exposure is informational, not operational : guests will ask, and wholesalers will notice. What most will miss: this is a slow-burn structural risk, not a one-off. The land-use pressure on Amboseli's edges will keep producing incidents until it eases — so a credible guest-comms posture is an asset you reuse, not a one-week fix. 🎯 So what, by segment 🦁 Bush: ready a short, factual guest note now (probe underway, park open, no visitor risk) and brief your guides. Candour, not silence — and don't discount into a story that doesn't threaten the experience. 🏙🏖 City/Beach: minimal direct exposure, but multi-park itineraries routing through Amboseli should carry the same honest line. --- 📋 THE BOARD ✈️ CONNECTIVITY — Uganda Airlines confirmed Accra from 27 Oct (4×/week, ~US$750 return) and Kigali from 18 Nov (daily, ~US$370 return — under RwandAir's ~US$450), building Entebbe as a hub. The Kigali link is the one to watch: it makes twin-hub Uganda–Rwanda gorilla circuits genuinely seamless. (The EastAfrican, ~5 Aug.) 💰 COST / STILL TRUE — EPRA holds Nairobi diesel at KSh222.86/L to 14 Aug; next review 14 Aug (watch the generator/transfer reset). Advisory board unchanged: Uganda US Level 4 , Kenya Level 2 , TZ & Zanzibar Level 3 . 🕓 HELD — AfDB's reported €156m Arua Airport upgrade, and talk of an expanded EAC single tourist visa, are not yet verified or gazetted — we'll run them when they are. 🔗 This edition on the web: 💼 Today's Big Read on LinkedIn: --- 📌 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Tue 11 Aug, Evening KWS is probing the deaths of 16 elephants in the Amboseli–Kimana landscape (Jun–Jul), with preliminary toxicology pointing to cyanide from suspected agrochemical misuse. records.title: Expert Brief: East Africa keeps announcing record arrivals. The number that should worry owners is where those guests come from — not how many there are.
records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Morning Brief Monday 10 August 2026 Expert Brief: East Africa keeps announcing record arrivals. The number that should worry owners is where those guests come from — not how many there are. --- 🌅 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Mon 10 Aug, Morning Quiet news morning. One Expert Brief, then the board. 1️⃣ THE RECORD THAT HIDES A RISK — READ YOUR SOURCE-MARKET MIX, NOT YOUR ARRIVALS LINE Every headline this year says the same thing: records. Zanzibar cleared 917,167 arrivals in 2025 (OCGS). Tanzania banked US$4.41bn in tourism earnings, up 13% (NBS, 2025). Kenya reports ~7.9m visitors. The applause is deserved. It is also the wrong thing to be watching. Look underneath Zanzibar's boom and you find a single load-bearing pillar: Europe supplied 61.9% of June arrivals (43,105 of 69,605) and 69.5% in January (OCGS, June figure released ~12 Jul). One region, most of your bookings. That is not a franchise — it's a bet on one continent's disposable income and one continent's risk appetite. What everyone is missing: a record-arrivals headline is not validation, it's a concentration warning. And you don't have to imagine the shock — it's live. Uganda sits at US Level 4 "Do Not Travel" (State Dept, 5 Aug) and the US CDC Section 362 entry order (renewed 13 Jul, next call ~12 Aug) has effectively frozen one Western source market for the Uganda/DRC corridor overnight. A single government notice did that. A European recession would do the same to a coast that leans 62–70% on Europe. The hedge already works — someone's proven it. Tanzania grew Chinese arrivals from 33,000 to 82,000 in two years through Mandarin-language outreach. Deliberate diversification, not luck. 🎯 So what, by segment 🏖 Beach: most exposed. Build Gulf/India/intra-Africa shoulder fill now — language, OTA and payment rails ready before the next Western wobble, not after. 🦁 Bush: the Uganda freeze shows how fast one advisory empties a source market. Court Gulf/India feeder demand on the new Doha/Dubai lift; hold rate through a Western gap rather than discounting. 🏙 City: MICE and intra-African business travel are your natural diversifier — MKTE (Oct), FHS Africa Uganda 2027, ICCA Kigali 2027 are demand that doesn't depend on Western leisure sentiment. 🏷 Regional · All segments · Confidence: High (data dated & sourced) --- 📋 THE BOARD ✅ STILL TRUE — Uganda US Level 4 unchanged (State Dept, 5 Aug); TZ & Zanzibar US Level 3 since 31 Oct 2025. Uganda's 42-day Ebola all-clear completes ~28 Aug, but no entry rule has changed. Don't price a US-market rebound you can't yet see. 📅 WEEK AHEAD — CDC Section 362 order decision ~12 Aug ; EPRA Kenya fuel review ~14 Aug (petrol held at KSh214.03/L to 14 Aug, EPRA Jul review); Hotel Expo Kenya 19–21 Aug (KICC). 🎤 MICE WATCH — Hotel Expo Kenya, Nairobi/KICC, 19–21 Aug (city midweek bump). WTA Africa Gala, Zanzibar, 28 Aug (north/east coast compression, last week of Aug). 📡 RADAR — Upstream source poll returned nothing new in-window this slot; advisory board and outbreak status unchanged since the weekend. No exclusive to report. 🔗 This edition on the web: --- 📌 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Mon 10 Aug Read the quality of your demand, not the quantity. Zanzibar leans on Europe for 61.9% of June arrivals, 69.5% in January (OCGS). records.text: EA Hospitality Pulse — Midday Pulse Monday 10 August 2026 Expert Brief: Kenya just set an air-traffic record — and it was domestic travellers who set it, not the inbound long-haul market operators spend all their energy chasing. --- 🕛 EA HOSPITALITY PULSE — Mon 10 Aug, Midday Quiet news slot. One Expert Brief, then the board. 1️⃣ THE RECORD WAS SET AT HOME — READ YOUR DOMESTIC DEMAND AS A STRATEGY, NOT A DISCOUNT BIN Kenya moved a record 13.1 million air passengers in the year to June 2026 , up from 12.955m a year earlier — about 145,000 more travellers (KAA preliminary data, via Daily Nation, 6 Aug). The line that matters sits underneath it: domestic routes were roughly 41% of all traffic , and KAA MD Moses Wekesa says it was domestic travel that carried the record while international numbers softened under Middle East disruption. What everyone is missing: the record was set because international dipped, not alongside it. Domestic and regional demand is counter-cyclical to exactly the Western shocks — advisories, long-haul softness, recession fear — that empty a coast or a corridor overnight. Fly748, back flying scheduled routes since May, is running strong Nairobi–Mombasa and Ukunda/Diani loads this school holiday, one-way fares from KSh 7,700 (Tuko, 6 Aug). That is real, growing, FX-proof demand — and most inbound-tuned properties are set up to miss it. 🎯 So what, by segment 🏖 Beach: the direct beneficiary. Package resident/school-holiday weekend rates, make sure M-Pesa and local rails work, and list where Kenyans actually book. This demand doesn't read a State Department bulletin. 🦁 Bush: your EAC-resident tier is the counter-cyclical floor under Western advisory risk — hold it as a revenue line, not a discount dump. 🏙 City: the record ran on a hub whose domestic legs grew while international slowed. Domestic corporate + MICE (Hotel Expo 19–21 Aug, MKTE Oct) is the compounding book. 🏷 Kenya · All segments · Confidence: High (data dated & sourced) --- 📋 THE BOARD ✅ STILL TRUE — Uganda US Level 4 (State Dept, 5 Aug); TZ & Zanzibar US Level 3 since 31 Oct 2025.
